INITIAL_EXPLORATION.name: INITIAL_EXPLORATION
INITIAL_EXPLORATION.objective: Observe how individual objects affect the detector.
guidelines: Test each object individually: place A, B, C, D, E on the detector one at a time
Record whether each individual object activates the detector
Remove the object before testing the next one to get clean observations
Pay attention to any inconsistencies when testing the same object multiple times

OBJECT_RELEVANCE_SCREENING.name: OBJECT_RELEVANCE_SCREENING
OBJECT_RELEVANCE_SCREENING.objective: Narrow down which objects are involved in the rule by systematic elimination.
guidelines: Test each object individually first — place A, B, C, D, E on the detector one at a time and record the result
Track a scorecard: for each object note ACTIVATES / DOES NOT ACTIVATE / INCONCLUSIVE
Test pairs that mix suspected relevant and irrelevant objects to confirm or ELIMINATE candidates
Once you have eliminated at least 1 object OR found 2+ activations, move on to COMBINATION_TESTING
Do NOT test the same pair or group twice in a row — each test should give you new information

transitions.condition: After eliminating at least 1 object or finding 2+ activations
If results are confusing, go back to individual tests

COMBINATION_TESTING.name: COMBINATION_TESTING
COMBINATION_TESTING.objective: Discover how object combinations and arrangements affect activation.
guidelines: Test different groupings of objects on the detector
Vary not just which objects are present, but how you arrange and sequence them
Compare results across different configurations
If a configuration that should work doesn't, consider what else might matter
BRANCHING: If you suspect order matters, transition to ORDER_TESTING. If you already have a hypothesis, transition to HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION.

transitions.condition: If you suspect order matters and want to test orderings
If you have enough evidence to form a hypothesis
If results are confusing, go back to screening

ORDER_TESTING.name: ORDER_TESTING
ORDER_TESTING.objective: Determine whether the order of objects matters for activation.
guidelines: Take your best candidate set of objects and test different orderings (e.g. A-B-C vs C-B-A)
Place objects in a specific sequence, observe, then rearrange and test again
Compare activation results across at least 3 different orderings of the same objects
If order does not seem to matter (same result regardless of arrangement), note this and move on
If you do not have a clear candidate set yet, skip ahead to RELIABILITY_TESTING
BRANCHING: If you want to test reliability, transition to RELIABILITY_TESTING. If you already have a hypothesis, transition to HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION.

transitions.condition: If you want to test reliability of your candidate rule
If you have enough evidence to form a hypothesis

RELIABILITY_TESTING.name: RELIABILITY_TESTING
RELIABILITY_TESTING.objective: Test whether your best candidate rule activates reliably.
guidelines: Take your best candidate rule and test it at least 3 times in identical conditions
Record whether activation is consistent (always activates) or intermittent (sometimes fails)
If results are inconsistent, the rule may be stochastic — note the approximate success rate
Test your rule's negation: remove one required object and confirm the detector does NOT activate
If you do not have a clear candidate rule yet, skip ahead to HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION

transitions.condition: After confirming reliability or detecting stochasticity

HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION.name: HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION
HYPOTHESIS_EVALUATION.objective: Evaluate your evidence to determine the causal rule.
guidelines: What rule type best explains ALL your observations?
Which specific objects are blickets?
Does order matter? Is the rule stochastic?
Are there observations that don't fit your current hypothesis?
If observations are inconsistent, consider whether factors beyond object identity might matter

transitions.condition: When you have a clear hypothesis
If hypothesis is unclear, test more combinations

VERIFICATION.name: VERIFICATION
VERIFICATION.objective: Confirm your hypothesis with targeted tests before submitting.
guidelines: Design a test that would distinguish your hypothesis from the next most likely alternative
If the test confirms, submit your answer
If the test disconfirms, reconsider your hypothesis
